question: The marked price of a jacket is ₹2400. If it is sold at a discount of 20%, find the selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price = (100% − Discount%) of Marked Price

SP = (100% − 20%) of 2400

SP = 80% of 2400 = (80 ÷ 100) × 2400

SP = 1920

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Marked Price (MP) = ₹2400 (100%)
 
 
 Selling Price = ? (80%)
 
 
 20%
 Discount
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹2400

Discount = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)]

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 2400 × [1 − (20 ÷ 100)]

⇒ SP = 2400 × [1 − 0.2]

⇒ SP = 2400 × 0.8

⇒ SP = 1920

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is an allowance given on the marked price of an article. It is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).
Formula: Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are given one after another on the marked price.
Equivalent discount for a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Profit & Loss Basics

While discount is calculated on Marked Price (MP), Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).
Formula: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.
